what: Protection equivalence (CORRECTED): minified+bundled JS via npm (with source maps rigorously excluded) and Bun compile provide ESSENTIALLY EQUIVALENT source protection in 2026 — ~1 min vs ~1-3 min to get the same bundled+minified JS content. Earlier claims of "15-30 min for Bun" were generous. Verified tools that extract Bun binaries in seconds: unbuned (github.com/vibheksoni/unbuned, zero-dep Python), bun-decompile.surge.sh (web app, drag-and-drop), bun-demincer (8-step auto pipeline with identifier recovery). After extraction, BOTH face identical deobfuscation — modern LLM-assisted tools (webcrack, humanify, Google CASCADE) reach 0.79 execution-correctness on minified JS for ~$0.01-0.50 per sample via GPT-4o-mini. Bun compile adds ~2 min of friction, nothing more. Canonical minified-npm shipping: `esbuild --bundle --platform=node --target=node20 --minify --external:better-sqlite3 --external:*.node --legal-comments=none` + `package.json` `files` allowlist + CI grep check for `.ts`/`.map`/`sourceMappingURL`/`src/` (Claude Code shipped source maps TWICE — Feb 2025 + Apr 2026 — because no CI check existed). Effort: ~1 day vs 2-3 weeks for binary. Binary's remaining justification: (a) zero-Node UX (user said don't care), (b) native-dep embedding beyond better-sqlite3 (N/A), (c) "real app" marketing feel. For source protection alone the binary migration is overkill vs minified-npm + javascript-obfuscator-on-hot-modules. The only genuine step-up from either JS approach: rewrite sensitive logic in Rust via napi-rs (Sentry/esbuild/swc/Turbo/Biome pattern) — raises RE cost to days-weeks.
why: Agent research corrected my prior timing claims (15-30 min for Bun was fiction — working extract tools take seconds). Also quantified the canonical minified-npm path. Critical for future binary-migration reviewers to see the corrected protection-equivalence framing before committing to the full binary plan.
